subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a first-class per-skill user preference contract, and if so should it be a markdown sidecar, structured `skills.entries` config, or no new core contract?
rationale: The request changes the public skill-loading and prompt-context contract, and the safe shape depends on maintainer intent around config-surface growth, SKILL.md precedence, watcher invalidation, and plugin/ClawHub boundaries.

options.title: Design Markdown Sidecar
options.body: Adopt a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar with explicit precedence and refresh semantics before implementation.

options.title: Use Structured Config
options.body: Add preference data under the existing config/schema path if maintainers want machine-readable per-skill settings instead of natural-language prompt context.

options.title: Decline Core Contract
options.body: Keep current `SKILL.md`, `skills.entries.config`, and global context behavior, leaving skill-specific conventions to user-managed skill copies or external packages.

recommendation.title: Design Markdown Sidecar
recommendation.body: Adopt a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar with explicit precedence and refresh semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across skill loading, docs, and the product-boundary policy that this decision touches.
